headline: Penpot adds AI integration with MCP server for programmatic design
summary: Open-source design tool now allows AI clients to read and modify designs, supporting self-hosted and remote setups.
details: Penpot, an open-source design and prototyping platform, is making waves by expressing designs as web standards like SVG, CSS, HTML, and JSON. This approach eliminates the proprietary lock-in of tools like Figma and ensures that copied code is what gets shipped, reducing design-to-implementation drift.

The platform natively supports CSS Grid and Flexbox, allowing designers to create responsive interfaces using the same layout models found in browsers. This direct mapping minimizes friction when translating mockups into actual code.

A significant new feature is the integration of an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server directly into the main Penpot repository. This enables any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot-style tools, to programmatically interact with Penpot design files.

The MCP server works with the real component tree, styles, and tokens within Penpot designs, allowing AI agents to understand and modify them without guesswork. The core of the MCP is written in TypeScript for type-safe interaction with the Penpot Plugin API.

Penpot emphasizes data ownership and control, offering both a hosted SaaS option and self-hosted deployments via Docker, Kubernetes, and other methods. This is particularly beneficial for teams in regulated industries like healthcare and finance who need to keep their design intellectual property on servers they control.

With first-class native Design Tokens, Components, and Variants, Penpot provides a single source of truth for design elements. When combined with the MCP server, the design system can serve as a direct context source for AI-generated code, streamlining workflows.

While Penpot may not yet match Figma's polish or prototyping depth, its focus on web-native output, AI integration, and data ownership makes it a compelling alternative for developers and teams prioritizing these aspects.

The MCP server supports both remote and self-hosted configurations. Users are advised to treat MCP keys as passwords and to start AI agents with read-only prompts before granting them permission to modify designs.
